checks.title: Labour and birth as positive feedback

mc.prompt: What makes cervical stretch and contraction a positive-feedback loop?
mc.answer: The response can increase the stretch that initiated it
mc.explanation: The classification depends on reinforcing the initiating change.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: The response can increase the stretch that initiated it
The response eliminates all contractions immediately
Oxytocin travels through a nerve rather than blood

mc.prompt: Which sequence correctly traces part of the birth control pathway?
mc.answer: Cervical stretch → sensory signalling → oxytocin release → uterine contraction
mc.explanation: The pathway connects receptor information, a central response, a circulating hormone and the uterine target.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Oxytocin → sperm formation → implantation → cervical stretch
Cervical stretch → sensory signalling → oxytocin release → uterine contraction
Cervical stretch → progesterone destruction of the fetus → ovulation
Pituitary contraction → neural milk production → gastrulation

writing.prompt: Trace the positive-feedback loop involving cervical stretch and oxytocin. Explain what makes it positive.
writing.model: Cervical stretch sends sensory information to the hypothalamus, promoting oxytocin release from the posterior pituitary. Oxytocin strengthens uterine contractions, which increase stretch. The response reinforces the initiating change. Delivery reduces the main stretch stimulus.

writing.prompt: Name and distinguish the three stages of parturition.
writing.model: During dilation the cervix widens. During expulsion the baby is delivered. During the placental stage the placenta is delivered. The stages are successive events, and delivery of the baby does not mean every stage is complete.
criteria: Identifies the relevant structures or quantities.

checks.title: Lactation and hormonal control after birth

mc.explanation: The anterior pituitary releases prolactin, which supports milk production.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.

mc.prompt: Why does placental delivery help permit increased milk secretion?
mc.answer: Estrogen and progesterone concentrations fall, changing their restraint on secretion
mc.explanation: The post-birth change in placental hormones permits stronger prolactin-supported secretion.
mc.cue: Trace the normal mechanism before choosing an answer.
options: Milk becomes a hormone that suppresses the hypothalamus
All prolactin is removed from the blood
The ovary releases a new acrosome
Estrogen and progesterone concentrations fall, changing their restraint on secretion

writing.prompt: Compare prolactin and oxytocin using their pituitary release sites and actions in lactation.
writing.model: Prolactin is released by the anterior pituitary and supports milk production. Oxytocin is released by the posterior pituitary and causes contraction around mammary secretory structures, helping eject milk. Producing milk and moving existing milk are different actions.

Explains the causal relationship or calculation, not just the final result.
Uses the stated evidence and avoids a stronger conclusion than it supports.

writing.prompt: Explain how the suckling response integrates nervous and endocrine signalling.
writing.model: Sensory receptors respond to suckling and send neural information to the hypothalamus. Central control influences hormone release, including prolactin and oxytocin. These hormones travel in blood to mammary tissues, where they support production and ejection.

videos.title: Labour and birth as positive feedback — video support
videos.purpose: Trace cervical stretch, neural signalling and oxytocin, then distinguish the three stages of parturition.
videos.fallback: Stronger contractions can push the baby more firmly against the cervix, increasing stretch. That additional stretch promotes further signalling and oxytocin release. The response reinforces the initiating change instead of opposing it. This is why the loop is called positive feedback. The word positive does not mean “good.” It describes the relationship between response and stimulus. Compare negative feedback, in which a response reduces a deviation or decreases the signal that initiated it. Delivery removes much of the cervical-stretch stimulus from this particular loop. A feedback explanation is incomplete unless it identifies what ends or limits the amplification.
videos.availability: Source hyperlink resolved syntactically; external playback not certified.
